title: Kubernetes Pod Lifecycle & Failure States

nodes.label: kube-apiserver
nodes.detail: Validates and persists Pod manifest state in etcd.

nodes.label: kube-scheduler
nodes.detail: Assigns unscheduled Pod to a healthy worker node.

nodes.label: kubelet Daemon
nodes.detail: Communicates with CRI to pull image and run containers.

nodes.label: Pod: CrashLoopBackOff
nodes.detail: Container repeatedly crashes immediately after startup. Backoff delay increases exponentially.

steps.title: Steady-State Health Monitoring
steps.action: Health check probe sends heartbeat polling requests every 5 seconds to kube-apiserver.
steps.why_traversal: Continuous active probing verifies that the instance is not merely powered on, but capable of processing application requests and database queries.
steps.narration: Hop 1: Health check probe continuously validates kube-apiserver response codes.

steps.title: Outage Trigger & Anomaly Detection
steps.action: Failure Trigger: kube-apiserver encounters threshold saturation or crash. Health check records 3 consecutive timeouts.
steps.why_traversal: Multi-probe threshold prevents transient network blips from triggering premature, expensive failovers.
steps.narration: Hop 2: Failure occurs on kube-apiserver. Probe signals unhealthy threshold breach to Load Balancer.

steps.title: Automated Failover & Traffic Eviction
steps.action: Control plane withdraws kube-apiserver from forwarding table and redirects incoming traffic to standby unit kubelet Daemon.
steps.why_traversal: Traffic reroutes in under 5 seconds across Google Andromeda SDN without DNS TTL delay or client reconfiguration.
steps.narration: Hop 3: Load balancer evicts kube-apiserver and reroutes active traffic to kubelet Daemon.

steps.title: Capacity Recovery & Auto-Healing
steps.action: Auto-Healing: Managed Instance Group recreates failed instance and synchronizes state with kubelet Daemon.
steps.why_traversal: MIG auto-healing restores full multi-zone redundancy, returning the cluster to balanced multi-active serving capacity.
steps.narration: Hop 4: Auto-healing restores capacity; kubelet Daemon serves traffic while new unit initializes.

scenarios.label: ImagePullBackOff (Registry Auth Failure)
scenarios.narration: Node service account lacks 'roles/artifactregistry.reader' or image tag does not exist. Kubelet fails image pull.
scenarios.root_cause: Node service account lacks 'roles/artifactregistry.reader' or image tag does not exist. Kubelet fails image pull.
scenarios.diverted_path: Normal request path is interrupted at kubelet Daemon, Pod: CrashLoopBackOff. Downstream components receive timeout errors or drop packets without acknowledgment, forcing client retries or failover redirection.
scenarios.blast_radius: All user sessions dependent on kubelet Daemon, Pod: CrashLoopBackOff experience elevated latency, HTTP 5xx errors, or severed connections.
scenarios.recovery: Deploy multi-region Anycast failover, cross-zone active-standby redundancy, automated health check eviction, and exponential backoff circuit breakers.

scenarios.label: kube-scheduler Network Degradation
scenarios.root_cause: Underlying Andromeda vSwitch queue saturation or hypervisor host maintenance causing 40% packet loss on kube-scheduler.
scenarios.diverted_path: Incoming TCP streams to kube-scheduler experience high retransmission rates and latency spikes up to 4500ms; gateway circuit breaker opens to shed load.
scenarios.blast_radius: Transactions processed by kube-scheduler slow down significantly; client applications encounter timeout errors.
scenarios.recovery: Configure client-side exponential backoff with full jitter; deploy Regional Managed Instance Groups with auto-healing and minimum 3-zone distribution.
scenarios.narration: Packet loss and connection timeouts detected on kube-scheduler. Circuit breaker trips to protect cluster.

scenarios.label: Quota exhausted
scenarios.root_cause: A project or regional quota reaches its allocation limit.
scenarios.diverted_path: Requests surface elevated latency, errors, or denied actions.
scenarios.blast_radius: Consumers of the affected resource or dependency.
scenarios.recovery: Reduce load, restore the dependency, and add a tested prevention.

purpose: Simulates Kubernetes Pod failure lifecycles: demonstrates CrashLoopBackOff root causes, kubelet restart backoff throttling, and automated scheduler recovery onto healthy cluster nodes.
routing_rationale: When application containers crash repeatedly, kubelet applies exponential backoff delays (10s to 300s) to prevent CPU starvation, while kube-scheduler evicts unresponsive pods to restore service SLAs.
summary: Simulates Kubernetes Pod failure lifecycles: demonstrates CrashLoopBackOff root causes, kubelet restart backoff throttling, and automated scheduler recovery onto healthy cluster nodes.
